Classify each of these player self-notes as SHALLOW or DEEP.

SHALLOW = only reports the outcome, the move played, or what's objectively
wrong with the position — a label or a fact about the board, not an
explanation of the player's own thinking
(e.g. "I blundered", "missed it", "this hangs my Rook for a Bishop",
"there was a discovered attack on my Queen that I missed").

DEEP = explains why the PLAYER made the move or missed the better one —
what they were thinking, focused on, or misjudging. Naming what's wrong
with the position or the resulting tactic (a fork, a discovered attack, a
weak rank) is NOT enough on its own — the note has to say something about
the player's own reasoning or mental error, even if brief or tentative.

A DEEP note doesn't need an explicit causal word like "because" — connecting
two facts is enough. "I saw the free rook" next to "missed the mate" already
explains the distraction that caused the miss.

Examples of DEEP:
- "I went to kick their Knight not seeing my Bishop was hanging." (explains
  what distracted them)
- "This is a calculation error, 2 attackers, one defender." (attributes
  the mistake to a specific miscount, not just stating the position)
- "I think I played a3 to protect it from capture." (states own intent,
  even tentatively)
- "I needed to get on the same file as the Queen to force it away."
  (explains the missed plan)

Examples of SHALLOW:
- "This hangs my Rook for a Bishop."
- "There was a discovered attack on my Queen that I missed."
- "I moved my queen into a forking square with my King."
- "This is a passive move, permitting my opponent to play Rc2, putting
  their rook on a very powerful rank."
- "It appears that the engine wants to make sure they don't have a bishop
  pair, but that's a guess." (explains the engine's logic, not the
  player's own reasoning)

For entries beginning with [3x3], the parts form one connected
self-analysis of a single decision (Why I played it = player's
intent, What was wrong = what was wrong with their move, Why the
better move is better = often the same underlying point restated,
Lesson = the takeaway). 'What was wrong' and 'Why the better move
is better' are board-fact questions by design — a factual answer to
either is NOT shallow. Classify the whole [3x3] entry as DEEP if
'Why I played it' or 'Lesson' contains genuine player-perspective
reasoning: what they were thinking, what they misread, or a specific
lesson that names the pattern (not just 'be more careful'). Classify
as SHALLOW only if all parts are bare board facts or generic filler
with no player angle.

Return one line per note: <index>: SHALLOW or <index>: DEEP.

0: I blundered my bishop by not checking captures.
1: Missed it.
2: I went to push my pawn not seeing the queen fork on f7.
3: There was a discovered attack on my queen that I missed.
4: [3x3] Why I played it: I wanted to activate my rook. | What was wrong: It walked into a pin on the e-file. | Why the better move is better: Re1 avoids the pin and keeps the rook active. | Lesson: Check for pins before rook moves.
5: I was focused on my queen not realising my knight was hanging.
6: This is a passive move, letting them seize the open file.
